messages.author: 3eaf9abccea468e2
messages.subject: Modification indices
parts:
Hello!

I'm currently learning SEM and I have used lavaan for course assignments. For this weeks assignment, I made a while loop that inserts one modification index (the one with highest mi value) per step in the model until certain statistical significance condition is reached.

I got into trouble as the highest value was for such equation that already existed in the model in another form. So in the model I have included 'F5 =~ DEC1 + DEC2' but modindices suggests to include 'F5 =~ DEC1' which leads to duplicate model element error.

So my question is whether there is way to exclude such duplicates. It doesn't seem that there's such option for modindices.

Cheers,

Antti

messages.author: 671b14edc9322fa7
messages.subject: Re: Modification indices
parts:
Hi

First of all, you should not be doing that. (Unless the assignment was to mindlessly modify the model.) Blindly following modification indices will lead to capitalization on chance and almost certainly incorrect model specification. 

Lavaan fixes the first factor loading to 1 by default to scale the LV. See the lambda matrix. 

inspect(fit)
You can free the loading by

F5 =~ NA*DEC1 + DEC2

Mikko

messages.author: 99a06696c483481a
messages.subject: RE: Modification indices
parts:
Antti—

    Mikko’s advice was sound.  While it might be possible to do what you request, it would be a very bad idea.

     Different constrained parameters can be tied to the same discrepancy in fit.  (For instance, here, that loading may be tied to the variance or residual variance of the factor.)  The modification indices are a blunt, dumb way to address the issue.  You can use them as pointers, to help you grasp the nature of the problem, but then you have to use what you know about your model and your situation to extract meaning out of the information.

--Ed Rigdon

messages.subject: Re: Modification indices
parts:
Hi

I do not understand what you mean by "overlapping”. When I change this
F5 =~ DEC1 + DEC2
to this
F5 =~ NA*DEC1 + DEC2

The parameter is freed. (Check parameter number 8 in the freed lambda.) This makes the model non-indentified, so it cannot be meaningfully estimated. There is no guarantee that following modification indices will keep the model identified. These are calculated based on partial derivatives of one parameter as a time keeping others fixed.

Mikko

messages.author: ad188126f9138663
messages.subject: re: Modification indices
parts:
Antti,
Here is a self-contained script that may illustrate what you are
describing, if I understand you correctly.

#Filter modification indices by model parameter variables.

#Fit example.
require(lavaan)
example.mod <- '
A~B
B~C
C~B+D'
example.cov <- matrix(1,ncol=4,nrow=4) + diag(4)
dimnames(example.cov) <- list(LETTERS[1:4],LETTERS[1:4])
example.N <- 500
example.fit <- lavaan(model=example.mod, sample.cov=example.cov,
sample.nobs=example.N, auto.var=TRUE)
inspect(example.fit, 'list')

# Filter MIs
mod.list <- inspect(example.fit, 'list')
mod.pairs <- mapply(c,mod.list$lhs,mod.list$rhs,SIMPLIFY=FALSE)
mod.L <- length(mod.pairs)
mi.fit <- modificationIndices(example.fit)
mi.pairs <- mapply(c,mi.fit$lhs, mi.fit$rhs,SIMPLIFY=FALSE)
mi.L <- length(mi.pairs)
redundant.mat <- matrix(NA, nrow=mi.L, ncol=mod.L)
for(i in 1:mi.L){
for(j in 1:mod.L){
redundant.mat[i,j] <- !identical(sort(unlist(mi.pairs[i])),
sort(unlist(mod.pairs[j]))
)
}
}
mi.index <- apply(X=redundant.mat, MARGIN=1, FUN='all')
mi.fit[mi.index,]

Keith
------------------------
Keith A. Markus
John Jay College of Criminal Justice, CUNY
http://jjcweb.jjay.cuny.edu/kmarkus
Frontiers of Test Validity Theory: Measurement, Causation and Meaning.

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Modification indices
parts:
On 11/24/2014 10:42 AM, Antti Simola wrote:
> Thank you so much Keith!
>
> That's exactly what I had in mind and I think it would be a nice
> addition for modindices() function to have that filtering as an option.

As it happens, the modindices() function in the dev version of lavaan
(0.5-18.748 or higher) has some additional output options:

- sort=TRUE will sort the mi's from large to small
- maximum.number=10 will only show the first 10 rows
- minimum.value=5 will only show value for which mi>5
- op="=~" will only show factor loadings

so you do things like:

modindices(fit, sort = TRUE, max = 4)

or

modindices(fit, op = c("=~", "~"), min = 3.0)

The only issue (in 0.5-18) is that you will not get modification indices
(yet) for constrained parameters in your model (eg, if you have equality
constraints).

Yves.
